metadata.technology_reasoning: The smartphone application processor SoC package is the dominant form used in nearly all modern smartphones as it integrates CPU, GPU, modem, and other key functions into a single chip, optimizing performance and power efficiency. These SoCs come as complete packages ready for integration onto the smartphone mainboard, making them the industry standard in 2024.

components.reasoning: The silicon die hosting the central processing units and graphics processing units is the core functional element of the SoC, always present and separate from the package substrate.
Most smartphone SoCs include an integrated modem module for cellular connectivity as a distinct functional block within the package, though some variants may exclude or separate this.
Smartphone SoC packages often integrate or package on package with DRAM memory chips to enhance performance, typically as a separate memory die or dies included in the package or stacked vertically.
Many SoC packages include or integrate power management ICs to manage voltage and power delivery, though in some designs this PMIC may be a separate package externally.
The substrate provides mechanical support and electrical interconnections for the SoC die and any stacked memory, a separate manufactured component essential to the package.

components.component: Ball Grid Array (BGA) or Flip-Chip Solder Balls
components.reasoning: These solder balls provide the electrical and mechanical interface between the SoC package and the smartphone PCB, standardized and always present as a distinct component of the package.
Encapsulation protects the die and internal components within the package from environmental damage, temperature, and mechanical stress, standard in all packages.
